To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new method has been developed that allows the preparation and sequencing of small amounts of protein or peptides, with high fidelity and low backgrounds, from SDS‐PAGE gels.
a preparative method for protein and peptide sequencing has been described.

a simple and rapid method has been developed for the sequencing of proteins, which is based on in situ staining of the proteins during preparative SDS‐PAGE, the use of microconcentrating devices to repeatedly concentrate the stained proteins onto small discs of PVDF, and the use of a dye to monitor the elution process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for the identification of the amino acid sequence of proteins and peptides in a preparative mode.
the development and application of a new method for the preparation of proteins and peptides for direct amino acid sequencing.
developing new methodologies and technologies to enable the rapid and efficient sequencing of proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the method is reliable and reproducible, and that the yields of sequence information obtained are comparable with those obtained from the standard Edman chemistry, with a significant reduction in the amounts of protein required.

the method presented in this paper has the following advantages: (i) it is a simple and reliable method; (ii) it does not require expensive equipment or chemicals; (iii) it can be used for proteins and peptides; and (iv) it can be applied to both preparative and analytical SDS‐PAGE.

this methodology has been successfully employed in obtaining the N‐terminal and/or internal amino acid sequence of 14 different proteins, including the human and mouse p53 tumour suppressor gene products and a number of other purified proteins, and that the methodology has been successfully applied to the purification of proteins from crude cell extracts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are able to obtain high quality amino acid sequences from as little as 1–2 pmol of protein or 10–20 pmol of peptide, and that this method can be used in conjunction with other methods of protein purification and sequencing.
we have developed a reliable method to sequence proteins and peptides that is both rapid and inexpensive.
the procedure is a simple and reliable means of obtaining both internal and N‐terminal amino acid sequences from small amounts of proteins and peptides.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to sequence small amounts of purified proteins or peptides by using the PVDF disc as a support for adsorbing proteins and peptides, and that this method is particularly suitable when the proteins or peptides of interest are not abundant.
the methodology is simple and reliable and can be used for the sequencing of proteins from small amounts of purified material, and for the sequencing of peptides from SDS‐PAGE.

the use of microconcentrating devices, which have been developed to concentrate small amounts of peptides, can also be utilised for concentrating small amounts of proteins and peptides from SDS‐PAGE gels, with the advantage of being able to monitor the concentration visually and to obtain a high‐yield, low‐background sequencing signal.
